items.label: March 1991
items.sum: New editor Charles Dickinson revives the magazine nearly two years after Joe Coleman's death, explaining that this issue covers up to September 1990.
items.s: END OF BELGRAVIAN FAMINE New editor Charles Dickinson revives the magazine nearly two years after Joe Coleman's death, explaining that this issue covers up to September 1990. It is nearly two years since Joe Coleman passed away. At the time nobody could have known that the March 89 Edition of Belgravian was to be the last under his Editorship. That issue of the magazine was itself a fine tribute to a man who worked so hard for the good of others. You will read in this issue of the loss of many Belgravians and it brings home to all of us that a great Club such as ours cannot survive without the introduction of new faces. Fortunately you will also read of a new Younger Committee and the involvement of several of our stars giving their time and efforts in support of us all. In collating this Edition of the Belgravian I have decided to use material prepared in 89 although parts of it may have been overtaken by events in 90. To ease back into a more regular reporting situation I have set a cut off point at the end of the 1990 Track and Field Season, that is September 90. Hopefully it will not be too long before you are reading of events of Winter 90 and the 91 Season. Your new Editor Charles Dickinson Joe Coleman Joe Coleman former editor; died c.1989, March 89 edition was his last Charles Dickinson Charles Dickinson new editor

items.label: March 1991
items.sum: New treasurer Frank Ward reports healthy club finances and announces a Belgrave Harriers Hall Maintenance Fund.
items.s: A WORD FROM THE TREASURER New treasurer Frank Ward reports healthy club finances and announces a Belgrave Harriers Hall Maintenance Fund. I have recently inherited the duties of Treasurer. At present the Clubs finances are in a healthy state. This is due to the hard work and immense foresight of a few and the generosity of many. Our survival is not a divine right and all of us should strive to find ways to advance the Club. We must not only adapt to change which in itself is a great asset but we should lead. Due to past experience and with an eye on the future it has been decided to create a "Belgrave Harriers Hall Maintenance Fund". Donations can be sent to me or to the Hall and will be greatly appreciated. I hope I can follow the fine example set by my predecessors. On behalf of the members I would like to thank all those who give financial support to the Club, however small or large. Frank Ward Frank Ward Frank Ward Treasurer

items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Sue Porter, the club's first female General Secretary, introduces herself after taking over from Joe Coleman in January 1988.
items.s: SECRETARY'S ADDRESS / FORWARD / SCRIBBLINGS / REPORT Sue Porter, the club's first female General Secretary, introduces herself after taking over from Joe Coleman in January 1988. It is very pleasant to be able to take this opportunity to go into print. This is my first office as General Secretary and, so I am told, I am Belgrave Harriers' first female to hold this office. This is not surprising though as females have only been allowed to be members of the club since 1977. I took over the reins from Joe Coleman on the first of January 1988, and I am still getting to grips with the ins and outs of a prestigious athletics club, how its run, and how it fits in with regional and national athletics. I am trying to become familiar gradually with various sections of the club: road running; track and field; cross country etc. So far I've managed to extend out from my own section, race walking, towards the ladies section and even to running a 3000m race and throwing the javelin in the Womens Southern League. Unfortunately, some of my races clash with major fixtures in the mens section and it is not possible for me to spectate and support as often as I should wish. Timekeeping for the Thameside League and the Ladies Southern League also keeps me busy. It is very enjoyable, even though hard work and time consuming, but certainly not dull and boring. If circumstances allow I may be able to look forward to being General Secretary for the next few years at least; the record secretaryship is held by A.Harley at 34 years, only another 32 years to go! Needless to say, I am also proud to be a member of such a prestigious and historic club and to be involved as Belgrave starts its second hundred years. In a period when so much in athletics is changing it is important to continue to encourage grassroots athletics through schools and locally organised events. Continual upsurge of young potential in the area nourished by organised coaching schemes and supported by enthusiastic members can ensure an equally successful second hundred years for the club. I'm glad to be part of it ! ...........................Sue Porter..... items.sum: Profile of club president Bill Laws: his committee work since 1974, engineering career, running record and partnership with Leo Coy in building the track and field squad.
items.s: Bill Laws - PRESIDENT 1990. Profile of club president Bill Laws: his committee work since 1974, engineering career, running record and partnership with Leo Coy in building the track and field squad. It is sometimes difficult to realise that many of our officials hold down responsible jobs, so hard do they work on behalf of our active members. Bill Laws, our 89/90 President, has worked continuously on the Belgrave Committee since 1974 mainly as a result of a good natured provocation from Charlie Manning. He has held most offices including Hon. Sec. and Coaching Sec. He organised the Club Dinner for 5 years and edited the Belgravian for 6 years but is best known as part of a double act, partnered by Leo Coy, which in 10 years has taken our 'A' Track and Field Squad from 35th ranking to No. 2 in the country. During this time he persuaded the GLC to upgrade our home track to an all weather surface and obtained grants and acted as project manager for the Belgrave Hall rebuild in the late 70's. Bill is a graduate Mechanical Engineer who worked for British Steel for 17 years. In 1977 he established a private engineering Company developing new products for the Metallurgical Industries. In 1987 the Metals Society awarded him the Dowding Medal for his improvements to hot steel rolling and in 1989 his Company was one of only three U.K. companies to obtain both Queen's Awards for Techology and Export. Bill joined Belgrave in 1952 while at Emmanuel School. He moved away; his membership lapsed but he rejoined in 1963. His athletic achievements he would describe as average Club Standard. However in 1978 as a vet he achieved some success finishing 2nd in the Club 20 mile Championships, 5th in the Surrey Vets Cross Country and with Laurie O'Hara and Brian Gorman won the Southern Counties Vets 10 mile team Championship. He ran 54.36 for 10 miles and that year made our 12 stage relay team. He still has the ability to surprise and recently had the distinction (our Hon. Handicapper says 'Doubtful' distinction) of winning the Yacht 3 handicap in 2 consecutive years. But it is on the management side that Bill has made the biggest contribution. Let's hope his best is yet to come ! Bill Laws Bill Laws President 89/90; on committee since 1974; former Hon. items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Obituary of Joe Coleman (1911-1989), Belgrave walker from 1927, AAA and RWA competitor, later general secretary, editor of The Belgravian and 1984 club president, reprinted from Race Walking Record.
items.s: IN MEMORIUM. JOE COLEMAN (October 1911 - April 1989) Obituary of Joe Coleman (1911-1989), Belgrave walker from 1927, AAA and RWA competitor, later general secretary, editor of The Belgravian and 1984 club president, reprinted from Race Walking Record. Many of us saw Joe early in April, as usual busy helping things to run smoothly. We were all shocked to hear of his death in mid-April. He had been involved in athletics for over sixty years - almost a lifetime. Born in October 1911, he joined Belgrave Harriers in 1927 as a runner, taking part in handicap races, so popular in those days, and he was no mean shot putter. He then switched his attention to walking and gradually worked his way up the fields to become one of the country's leading performers over the shorter distances. He was a regular member of the very successful Belgrave teams before World War II and also figured in a winning team for the Nijmegan Shield in the RWA 20 miles. His dead heat with his brother, the late Len Coleman, in winning the RWA ten miles "junior" (based on performance) at Hampstead Garden Suburb in 1938, was a triumph he greatly enjoyed. He was a loyal Surrey County supporter, winning the ten miles walk in 1939 and going on to finish second in the inter-counties 10. In those days there was no senior championship at ten miles, and this event brought all of the countries' top men at this distance together. He was a regular competitor on the track, contesting the AAA Championships with distinction. Thanks to constant, hard and regular training, and attention to style, he gained a "Fowler-Dixon" award for style in the championships. Then came the 1939-45 war when he served in the R A F but with the post war resumption of championships he soon got back to form and when RWA decided to hold a senior ten miles championship Joe scored in the winning team. So he kept on for many years, helping many a newcomer with his advice. On retirement from racing he took up judging. Over recent years he got much involved in the administrative side of the club taking over the Hon General Secretary's job at short notice, a job he did with his customary good natured efficiency. He also took on the job of editing the club magazine "The Belgravian". His jovial and friendly manner will be missed by all who knew him. The respect in which he was held by Belgrave was demonstrated by his election to Life Membership, and in 1984 the ultimate honour of the Club Presidency. Gordon Doubleday (The above appeared in Race Walking Record and is re-produced by their kind permission). items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Tribute to Joan Goswell, who with her husband Jack ran a race walking results service for over 30 years and was made an RWA life member in 1986.
items.s: JOAN GOSWELL R.I.P Tribute to Joan Goswell, who with her husband Jack ran a race walking results service for over 30 years and was made an RWA life member in 1986. Joan was neither an athlete nor an official yet with her husband Jack she provided the sport of race walking over 30 years with a very reliable recording and results service. Joan probably attended more R.W.A. National Championships and Open races than many active competitors. I doubt if she saw many of these races except the start as she spent many, many Saturday afternoons tucked away in some small room often without heat or refreshment banging away at a typewriter in order to ensure that competitors could receive a complete result sheet shortly after the end of a race. I don't think that race walking fully appreciated the excellent service which Joan and Jack provided free of charge until it ceased a couple of years ago because of Joan's failing eyesight. Now it is no longer the norm to receive result sheets at Nationals in fact sometimes results are only available some days afterwards. Although Joan was a very quiet lady she was held in high esteem by walkers who recognised her as one half of a very unique partnership which did much for race walking. The presence of Jack at a race without Joan usually drew the comment, "where is Joan?". Rather belatedly in 1986 the Race Walking Association awarded Joan 'Life Membership', an honour which had been bestowed on her husband Jack in 1973. Joan was a great lady who for the benefit of others was generous with her talents and free time and who, with Jack, gave yeoman service to Belgrave Harriers, the Race Walking Association and the sport of race walking. Our condolencies to Jack on his great loss. John Keown Joan Goswell JOAN GOSWELL race walking results recorder for over 30 years; RWA Life Membership 1986 JOAN GOSWELL Joan Jack Jack Joan Goswell's husband; RWA Life Membership 1973 John Keown John Keown R.W.A. items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Obituary of marathon runner Bert Mitchell (1907-1989), donor of the Mitchell Shield, who was second in the Manchester to Blackpool Marathon in the late 1930s.
items.s: A.F. "BERT" MITCHELL (1907 - 1989) Obituary of marathon runner Bert Mitchell (1907-1989), donor of the Mitchell Shield, who was second in the Manchester to Blackpool Marathon in the late 1930s. We regret to announce the death of Bert Mitchell, donor of the Club's "Mitchell Shield" for the Belgrave Marathon Championship. It was in 1931 that Ken O'Kell signed up Alf Taylor and Bert Mitchell, after beating the former in a 1 mile race at AEC Southall. After moving to Ford's Dagenham in 1932, Ken discovered that both lads were also Ford workers. When Bert turned to marathon running he found that the alternating shift system at the works prevented him from training properly, particularly as he travelled by train from Wandsworth to Dagenham daily. He struck a bargain with his foreman. He could do a permanent early shift (6a.m to 2p.m) provided he agreed to produce 180 axle shafts a shift instead of the standard 160. So he left home at 3.30a.m and arrived home at 4.00p.m each day. He never grumbled, never sought promotion; always said how lucky he was to have a job and to have time to train. In the late thirties he achieved a second place in the prestigious Manchester to Blackpool Marathon. Because his fellow workers paid for his trip he wore a FORD Sports Club vest, a decision which brought a rebuke from that fiery little Belgrave Captain, Bert Footer! One of his most prized awards was a special oak plaque, formed and carved by the King's woodcarver from Windsor Castle oak, presented for the Windsor to Chiswick marathon. Bert was not one of our star runners in the highly successful teams of the thirties, but he was always there to provide back-up when needed. His will left a legacy of £100 to the Club: he always was a 100% Belgravian. With acknowledgements to Ken O'Kell A.F. "Bert" Mitchell A.F. items.sum: Obituary of long-distance walker Fred Rickards, a member for nearly 65 years, eight-time winner of the Police Barking to Southend Walk and member of many winning RWA teams.
items.s: F. RICKARDS Obituary of long-distance walker Fred Rickards, a member for nearly 65 years, eight-time winner of the Police Barking to Southend Walk and member of many winning RWA teams. We are sorry to learn of the passing of one of our oldest members, Fred Rickards, one of our long-distance walking "greats". He was over ninety and had been a member for nearly sixty-five years. We recall the number of wins he had in the Police Barking to Southend Walk - eight in all, 1924, '25,'26,'30,'32,'33,'35 and '39 and helping his team, K Divison to victory. He also had a great record as a team man, being in our winning teams in the R.W.A 20 miles Championship in 1925, '28,'38 and '39 and taking second individual place in 1934. He also helped the Club to win the Nijmegen Shield (for the complete team of eight) in '32, '38 and '39. Likewise in the 50 Kilos Championship he helped us to win in '34 (where he was third Individual), '35,'36 and '38. In addition he helped us to gain many team placings. He won the Club 20 miles Championship on a number of occasions, and had some fine performances on the London to Brighton Road to his name. On retirement from the Police he spent his last years living at Jarvis Brook, near Crowborough, in Sussex. He was of a sturdy build and a powerful walker. He took his sport seriously and trained hard and conscientiously for the big events. His cheerfulness and ready smile plus a warmth of character made him many friends and admirers. He recently wrote expressing his pleasure at seeing the successes of our track runners as shown on television. Obviously a great team man to the end. Its been great knowing you Fred, you have helped in no small way in making Belgrave the great Club that it is. Fred Rickards F. items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Obituary of Dick Towndrow (born 1908), cross-country and road runner who joined Belgrave in 1939 and won the 1948 Wigmore Open 15 miles.
items.s: R.F. TOWNDROW Obituary of Dick Towndrow (born 1908), cross-country and road runner who joined Belgrave in 1939 and won the 1948 Wigmore Open 15 miles. It is sad to think that Dick Towndrow died in September, a few weeks before attaining 50 years of membership of the Club. Born in 1908 and living at Barnes he enjoyed running in Richmond Park and on Wimbledon Common which he regarded as his "second-home". His first club was Ashcombe AC which had their Headquarters near the Sheen Gate of Richmond Park. Later they became amalgamated with St.George's Services A.C, but this combination didn't last many years and he then joined the Poly. A good cross-country and road runner he was a formidable opponent and had many fine runs to his credit. World War 2 broke out in September 1939 and in the November he joined us. He served in the Army and was able to continue his running. There were, of course, no championships but I remember a seven mile race over the old two lap Blackstaffe Shield course which he won. After the war he represented us in many races. His best effort must have been when he won the Wigmore Open 15 miles in 1948. This race was held over a hilly course from Parliament Hill and his time of 87m.20s. was a very good one for those days. In the mid-fifties he moved to Mere, near Warminster, Wiltshire. His enthusiasm for the Club was such that he continued his membership. A schoolmaster by profession he was a quiet modest and unassuming person, dedicated to his running and held in high regard by all. We have lost another of our long-standing stalwarts who many will remember with affection. Gordon Doubleday R.F. "Dick" Towndrow R.F. items.s: DANNY WISEMAN (18.12.44 - 22.08.88) Obituary of middle-distance runner David "Danny" Wiseman (1944-1988), who joined as a boy in 1954, ran 1:52.2 for 880 yards and won a Maccabiah Games silver. David "Danny" Wiseman died of cancer at the early age of 44 last August. Danny joined the Club in 1954 at the tender age of 9 years. In 1959 he was second in the Boys Medal Competition, taking both the 100 and 800 events. Alf Wilkins began coaching him in 1963, the year he first broke two minutes for the half mile. The following year he was a surprise winner at the NUTS winter track meeting at Hurlingham in a personal best of 1:54:4. He also represented Cambridge University against Oxford that year at the White City, a match which was televised live. He clocked a lifetime best of 1:52:2 for 880 yards in the 1965 Surrey Championships and gained a silver medal in the Maccabiah Games 800m. The following year he was elected secretary of the Cambridge University AC but owing to injury did not complete again in the varsity match. In 1973 Danny made a brief racing comeback and was very quickly into form. The following year he won the Club Championships in 1:54.7. He remained a keen follower of athletics and attended all the recent World and European Championships and was planning to visit both Gateshead and Barcelona for the European and World Cups before his illness became so bad. Our deepest sympathy is extended to his wife, Diane, and his two young daughters. items.sum: Obituary of miler Don Maclean, who died aged 57 after an accident; he set a Surrey Junior Mile record of 4:25.6 and ran 4:14.7 at Oxford.
items.s: DONALD MACLEAN Obituary of miler Don Maclean, who died aged 57 after an accident; he set a Surrey Junior Mile record of 4:25.6 and ran 4:14.7 at Oxford. We regret to record the death of Don Maclean who died recently following an accident. He was 57. Don and his brother were signed up for Belgrave by Tom Carter in 1948 when Don was 15 years old. Micky Pyer gave him a training schedule which soon began to show results, and the following season he ran three sub-5 minute miles. Improvement was dramatic the following year. He won the LAC Schools mile in the third fastest ever time of 4:28.2 (something special in those days), finished 2nd in the All-England Schools and beat Peter Driver in the Surrey Junior Mile with a record 4:25.6. He represented London versus Paris winning the 1500 metre and 2000 metres in the home and away fixtures. Following military service in Korea he resumed training in late 1954 and went to Oxford University where he studied philosophy, politics and economics. He gained a 'blue' over the country and reduced his mile time to 4:14:7; but a troublesome stomach ulcer plagued his performances after that and his form deteriorated steadily. However, he still produced some very good runs for the Club and could claim that he had never dropped out of a race. Don was an ardent Belgravian : the Club meant a great deal to him. Our sympathies are extended to Jennifer and her family. items.s: LAURISTON COTTAGE SOLD Arthur Whitehead leaves Lauriston Cottage after 54 years for Sedbergh; account of his post-war running, 1953 A.A.A. Marathon honours badge and the club's farewell presentation by Charlie Manning, with a photo of him in Sedbergh. After 54 years of residence at Lauriston Cottage ARTHUR WHITEHEAD has returned to the land of his youth, Sedbergh, in the heart of the Cumbrian Fells. Older members will recall running around the lawns of Lauriston House when Lady Fell, Arthur's step grandmother, was in residence. On her death the large house was demolished to make way for the housing estate which now occupies the land. Arthur retained the old stable block which, over the years, he converted to two dwellings and a running facility. It was in 1945 that he had returned to Lauriston after being badly wounded in Normandy. His unique determination to rehabilitate himself led to his joining Belgrave. Gradually he built his weight up from 6½ stone and with regular, though painful, training runs and early morning swimming in Queensmere he eventually turned to competition road-running. In 1953 Arthur achieved the performance that meant more to him than it could possibly mean to anyone else, he won a Belgrave Honours Badge in the A.A.A. Marathon of 1953. Following a successful completion of the London to Brighton Road Race he retired from competition to work for Belgrave and the newly formed Road Runners Club, of which he was a founder member. His contribution to our cross-country and road-running programme in the fifties and sixties was considerable, and his premises have always been at the disposal of Belgrave for the 12-stage relay and open '20'events. The Belgrave Committee presented him with a limited edition of a new book on the history of Wimbledon, which is so dear to his heart. The leather-bound boxed presentation copy contained the following tribute: "To Arthur, in appreciation of your 44 year long association with Belgrave Harriers (1945 - 1989)" (Signed) W.R. Laws, President. ARTHUR'S SEDBERGH RETIREMENT Charlie Manning visited Sedbergh in late Feb. and made the presentation on the Club's behalf. The photograph shows Arthur (now 77 years) in Finkle Street with his house in the terrace behind. Arthur writes :- "Today I had a delightful surprise visit from Charlie Manning who brought with him the magnificent gift from Belgrave who are much too generous to me. The book is a wonderful record of Wimbledon and will always bring back happy memories. Every good wish and many thanks". For those interested Arthurs new address is :- [address withheld]. items.s: grapevine Club gossip column: a birth for the Obengs, Darren Mead's wedding and move to Norfolk Gazelles, Kevin Sturman's photography business, bar income and discos, a bar joke, Sue Porter's change of name and Andrew Lloyd's foot operation. Congratulations to Sharon and Ernest Obeng on the birth of a 6½lb boy. John Regis and Marcus Adam should look out for the name Adam Obeng in about 15 years time. Our somewhat belated best wishes go to Donna and Darren Mead on their wedding. They have moved back to Norfolk where they have set up home. Sadly Darren has found that to continue as a first claim member of Belgrave is not practical and he has joined Norfolk Gazelles. We wish him all the best. Kevin Sturman has returned from the U.S.A. where he has been working as a Professional Photographer. He is setting up as a freelance photographer in the U.K. undertaking all types of industrial, fashion and sports assignments. Kevin has supplied most of the photo's in this edition of the Belgravian. If you need his Professional Services you can ring him on [phone number withheld]. Bar income has returned to more respectable levels since Stuart Paton was successfully headhunted as our Hon.Social Sec. A series of Discos at which he was aided and abetted by John Gladwin and Gary Staines have proved wildly successful so keep an eye open for some more outrageous entertainment from the terrible trio. See notice board (Page 67) Serving behind the bar at Belgrave Hall can be quite an experience. It is quite easy to mishear a conversation. One story circulating is that at the time of the fall of the Berlin wall one punter was heard to remark " I see the Honecker's are off!"."Can't understand that"said the barman"I only put a new barrel on last night". Have you spotted that we have not changed our Gen. Hon. Sec. but that Sue has changed here name. Our very best wishes to Sue and Harry Porter.(See Page 63). Following a tremendous track season Andrew Lloyd has returned home for an enforced break. He will be having another foot operation to remove bone injured several years ago in a car accident. We wish him a speedy recovery. items.s: ATHLETES FOOTNOTES Short notes on athletes: Lenny Paul's appointment as team captain with the sectional captains, and Philip Goedluck returning to sprinting. Lenny Paul's top posting. As we enter the '91 T & F Season Lenny Paul takes up a new post as 'A' team Captain. The Sectional Captain's jobs remain and are :- Sprints - John Regis, Throws - Abi Ekoku, Jumps - Derek Browne, Distance - Stuart Paton. Philip Goedluck gets serious. After 3 years building his career in the Fire Service Philip Goedluck has decided to concentrate for a while on his sprinting. Having run 5th in the Junior World Championship 200m some 4 years ago Philip would be the first to admit he has not fulfilled early promise. He has moved to coach John Isaacs and now trains with Marcus Adam and John Regis. items.sum: Harry Porter's review of the Ladies Section's 1989 season: international honours, UK rankings, relegation in the Women's Southern League through injuries and a lack of juniors, and thanks to helpers and officials.
items.s: The Ladies. Harry Porter's review of the Ladies Section's 1989 season: international honours, UK rankings, relegation in the Women's Southern League through injuries and a lack of juniors, and thanks to helpers and officials. 1989 was highlighted by three ladies gaining international honours: Andrea Coore - Great Britain : Long Jump Morag Andrews - Scotland : Cross Country Sian Spacey - Wales : Racewalking Well done Andrea, Morag and Sian! However, our success in the Women's Southern League was dulled by injuries to both sprinters and mdiddle distance Seniors and also by having only a few Junior Ladies. The Schools' meetings held in Battersea Park over the early summer attracted a few more girls, and we strengthened our links with local schools. We also had three Senior Ladies appearing in the UK 1989 rankings: Wendy Dunsford : Shot Andrea Coore : Long Jump Ese Oshivire : Heptathlon Well done Wendy, Andrea, and Ese, who also holds the British Universities Record for the Heptathlon. Again due to injuries, 1989 was the first time in three years' competitions that Belgrave Ladies failed to reach the semifinals of the GRE cup. Scoring in the Women's Southern League matches is by both Senior and Junior Ladies, unlike the position in the Men's Southern League matches which are for Senior Men only. This year, our lack of Juniors together with injuries to the Senior Ladies meant that Belgrave were relegated to Division Three for 1990, after four years in Division Two. This has also happened to three or four other London clubs who similarly suffer from a lack of Juniors, or even Juniors but a lack of Seniors. I have each year tried to have the rules changed, but so far nothing has been done to help clubs in the same position as us. We cannot rely on just one or two people to strengthen the Ladies Section, but need to encourage a concerted effort from all sections of the club, both normal club members and also committee members. The Ladies Section has a fine supporting group of Mums and Dads, officials and helpers. My thanks go to all those who regularly support the Ladies Team, but especially to Wyn Shepherd and Jean Hutchinson who compile the results for home matches, Thameside League and others, Derek Jones who organises fixtures for Thameside and Interclub meetings as well as being our field official, Derek Crookes, our tireless timekeeper/marksman assisted by Sue Morrison, Arthur Penny, our perennial home base starter and assistant Eric Crutcher, plus the field team of Johnny Morris, Ken Giles, Ray James and Carl Lawton. And a very special 'thank you' to my assistant Cynthia James, and the support of her family, Ray, Andy and Richard, and Chris and Jenny Christou. There are also members of other clubs who also keep with our matches, among these John Gebbels and Cyril Gittens especially. Well done everybody and thank you all very much for your support throughout the year, and good luck for 1990; we will need it! items.sum: Humorous piece picking Belgrave's best 12 road runners for the AAA road relay as wines from an Oddbins brochure, each with a mock tasting note, plus 'Gran Reserves'.
items.s: A CASE OF 12. Humorous piece picking Belgrave's best 12 road runners for the AAA road relay as wines from an Oddbins brochure, each with a mock tasting note, plus 'Gran Reserves'. You may have read that Oddbins were voted Wine Merchants of the year in 1989.At Xmas their colourful brochure dropped onto the mat and its contents made mouth watering reading. As usual there was the standard hyperbole. Strangely many of the descriptions seemed appropriate to our Road Running members and as my mind wandered yet again to the day when we might get our 12 best into the AAAs road relay I found the team selecting itself- and quite a presentation pack it made. Judge for yourself. 1. Thetford Mead 68. -High quality performer. Early hint of class now being confirmed. Stunning. Will mature further to give much pleasure in years ahead. 2. Vouvray Paton 84. -Light and sparkling. Vibrant. Refreshing up-front with a long aftertaste. Low alcohol makes it suitable for parties. 3. Chateau la Foote 63. -A fine performer with no delusions of grandure. Excellent balance. Considered by many to rank as best buy. 4. St Julien Chaston 68. -A favourite rouge with plenty of tannin(g). Elegant and rich with an excellent body. 5. St Matthew Chaston 67. -The second label of the famous Welsh lineage. Little to distinguish from its more up-front relation. A fine buy. 6. Coonawara Staines 87. -A tough customer produced by the best of Aussie knowhow. Travels well. A rarely seen vintage but a prize winner none the less. 7. Frascati Bizio Superiore.DOC. 85. -A clean and natural white- fresh from Italy. Careful preparation is now beginning to pay off with a good chance of true greatness. A long term investment. 8. Zinfandel Gladwin Blush 88. -Proves that local products can take on the best. Gold medallist. Classy,attractive,clean and quite long. Now making a comeback after several poor vintages. 9. Ward Cru Bourgeois 85. -Fruity and pleasant but can be unpredictable. Pushing some of the better names for recognition. Needs company for the best results. 10. Paul Masson Evans 88. -Not a Californian but a Northerly British equivalent. Distinct local flavour which has surprised Continental experts with its fine finish. 11. Gilbey NV(Non Vintage). -Ripe, ready now, will soon be over the hill. Full aromatic flavour-not to be sniffed at. 12. Clos de Hayes 89. -A good year following a poor growth. Frequently up and down but should eventually reward those who can wait. GRAN RESERVES. Also recommended with a good chance of making the top 12. Saunders Shiraz 88. A newcomer who has outclassed several established names. Sinclair 2nd Cru 84. Yet to obtain the standard of its illustrious forebear. Could be stunning. Penfold LLoyd 88. Another great from Oz. Finding it difficult to get UK recognition. Needs time(about 3 months). Schloss Maynard 86. Top of the list at Waitrose for past few years. Bold and inviting. Darrell Mead 88. Disappointing year. Better 87"s Adams Reserve 89. May confirm earlier promise but avoid the 89"s. Fonseca Forrester 89. Ripe and round. Full bodied. And there is more being laid down right now. But that is another story. items.s: NATIONAL 12 STAGE RELAY - SUTTON PARK Report and leg-by-leg results of Belgrave's return to the National 12 stage road relay at Sutton Park: 17th in 1989 and 14th in 1990, led by Paul Evans's fastest long leg, with winners Tipton and the fastest legs in both years. The last time we considered ourselves good enough to turn out in the National Road Relay was in the early 70's when we finished 17th. By coincidence our 1989 return resulted in a similar position while in 1990 we improved to 14th despite the absence of 5 of our winning Southern team. Paul Evans astounded everyone by running the fastest long leg by a 20 sec. margin while Andy Lloyd made a welcome return to finish 2nd fastest on the short leg followed by Justin Chaston 3rd fastest and a somewhat surprised Stuart Paton in 6th fastest place on the short leg. John Hobbs, Martin Lake, Gary Pitts and Mike Webb all acquitted themselves well at this their first taste of the big time. They should be well fired up for next year. Our continuing improvement augers well for the National 6 stage and for next year's 12 stage - that is if the athletes get together and decide to give these races priority. Whatever the future 1990 will be remembered as the year when Belgrave again became a name to be respected on the Road. April 15th 1989 April 28th 1990 1. D. Mead 26.07 ( 8) 2. S. Paton 14.29 ( 4) 3. Black 14:38 This event was only given the go-ahead half an hour before the official start time of 11am - the reason being the sinking of the Thames riverboat 'Marchioness' during the previous night. As a result, it was decided that although the event would take place, no results would appear in the national or local press. Belgrave 'A' team ran well to take second place behind a strong team from Woodford Green who were never troubled. Bels did have a fright though, as, VPH closed to within 1 second at the final changeover. The City Police laid on a magnificent buffet lunch for the competitors after the race and a lucky few were shown around the stables before leaving. items.sum: Profile of Paul Evans, who joined Belgrave in 1988 and in 1990 won his third consecutive Southern Counties 10,000m title and the Southern 3000m in a record, his first British vest and five stages of the Sun Life Great Race on his way to 5th overall. Illustrated by the 1990 British Athletics League programme cover featuring him.
items.s: PAUL EVANS Profile of Paul Evans, who joined Belgrave in 1988 and in 1990 won his third consecutive Southern Counties 10,000m title and the Southern 3000m in a record, his first British vest and five stages of the Sun Life Great Race on his way to 5th overall. Illustrated by the 1990 British Athletics League programme cover featuring him. 1990 has seen Paul Evans, one of Belgrave's newer members, poised to make a great international breakthrough in athletics. He is perhaps best known for his fine performance recently in finishing 5th in the 20-stage Sun Life Great Race. However it should not be overlooked that Paul also headed the 1990 road 10,000m rankings and only missed the European Championship 10,000m qualifying time by a few seconds. Paul came to athletics relatively late in life, only starting to train seriously in 1985 after running 33 minutes in a local 10 km fun run in his home town of Lowestoft. This was when he was 24. By the time he joined Belgrave in October 1988 he already had the reputation of being a very successful road runner, and had been Eastern Counties cross country champion. In the summer of 1989 Paul established himself as an important member of the Belgrave British League track team often racing 800, 1500 and 5000m for the club and picking up valuable first place points. Paul begun 1990 with an impressive 2nd place in the New Year's Day Morpeth to Newcastle road race, just behind Paul Cuskin, but claiming the scalps of Steve Jones, Steve Brace and Geoff Wightman amongst others. Unfortunately a period of injury forced him to miss the major cross country championships and the World cross country trial. But in April Paul returned with an excellent 2nd fastest long stage in the Southern 12-stage relay, just behind Gary Staines and helping the Belgrave team to victory. Shortly after this he ran the fastest leg in the National 12-stage. On the track Paul won his third consecutive Southern Counties 10,000m title at the end of April running a solo 28:36.2. A week later he broke the Southern Counties record in winning the 3000m in 7:58.82. He was rewarded with his first British International vest and won the 10,000m against Finland in Helsinki on June 7th. Here he lowered his PB to 28:18.94 a massive 45 second improvement from the previous year and only seconds away from the European qualifying standard of 28:15. Paul was disappointed not to make the standard or the British team for Split. He thought possibly too many hard track races had taken their toll as he finished only 14th in the U.K. trial at Gateshead. However, by August he had returned to his best form producing the top U.K. 10 km road time in 1990 with 28:29 in Copenhagen. Paul was uncertain whether to run in the 20-stage Sun Life Great Race in early September, but was persuaded by close friends and family. For the first week he mainly stayed in the pack not contesting the leadership. The eighth day, however, proved to be a landmark in Paul's athletic career. He had been given an ultimation by his employer to return to work on this day or lose his job. Paul decided to stay and run. He produced his first remarkable stage win that day which was followed by victories on stages 12, 14, 15 and 17. He was only just pipped at the post in the final stage at Westminster. His efforts were rewarded with a total of £15,000 prize money for his 5th overall place. As the first Brit home he had averaged sub 5 minute mileing for the whole 240 miles. Will this success in the Great Race point to future marathon career ? Although many people think so, Paul is still very determined to break 28 minutes for 10,000m on the track, a time so rarely achieved by British athletes. We wish Paul luck and are very glad that he is running in Belgrave colours. Captured for posterity on the front cover of the British League Programme in 1990, Paul Evans went on to be 1st Brit. in the Great Race from Glasgow to London in which he averaged sub 5 minute miling. items.sum: Round-up of Belgrave veterans' 1988-90 cross country, track and road achievements, led by Charles Dickenson, Laurie O'Hara, Leo Lyons, Alan Painter and Mike Newton.
items.s: Veterans Round-up of Belgrave veterans' 1988-90 cross country, track and road achievements, led by Charles Dickenson, Laurie O'Hara, Leo Lyons, Alan Painter and Mike Newton. There were some very good results in the Cross Country Road, and Track. In the Cross Country 88/89 season Charles Dickenson was very good with a win in the Surrey 2nd in the V.A.C. Championship, 2nd in a Cross Country race at Haywards Heath and well placed in the Southern Vets in which we were also placed in the Team events. Leo Lyons in the Southern Vets Cross Country League was the individual winner. Tony Stone won the 45 group in the V.A.C. Championship. On the Track Laurie O'Hara did a hat trick in the 1500m (the V.A.C, Southern Vets and National Vets). Alan Painter had a fine win in the American Banks Vets mile at Chrystal Palace on September 3rd with a time of 4.50. On the Road Charles Dickenson had some good races - 2nd Vet in the 1988 Hogs Back, 2nd Vet in the Drapers Tool 10K. He also ran the second fastest leg in the Cranford Relay. He ran 2:33 in the London Marathon and also won both the V.A.C. 5 and 10 miles championship. He won the City 10 on New Years day (he actually was second but as the winner, Marcello Bizin had entered on the day which did not count). In the older age group Laurie O'Hara won his age group at Battersea Vets, and that was after a road accident plus some fine runs (races unknown). Also Mike Newton has made a very good change to short distance running after concentrating mainly on marathons. He won the over 50 age group in the T.V.H. 10K and had a very good run in the Southern Vets relay. He was also placed 3rd in the Surrey Vets in October '89. Unfortunately we missed 2 of our best members for 89/90 Cross Country season. Charlie Dickenson went away on a world tour and will be returning in August '90. Alan Painter had to have a hernia operation, and is now slowly coming back to his racing fitness. items.sum: Bill Laws's day-by-day account of the 1990 Commonwealth Games in Auckland, where Belgrave athletes won 4 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze, and of patron Eddie Kulukundis's hospitality; with two photos.
items.s: COMMONWEALTH GAMES REPORT - (or 'The Eddie Experience!) Bill Laws's day-by-day account of the 1990 Commonwealth Games in Auckland, where Belgrave athletes won 4 gold, 2 silver and 1 bronze, and of patron Eddie Kulukundis's hospitality; with two photos. The best laid plans of mice and men! The start was inauspicious. Thursday 25th January turned out to be the day of the big storm. Gatwick Airport was closed and our New Zealand Airways flight eventually took off 22 hours late. As a result I missed the heats of the 100 and Gary's epic run in the 10,000m. Ron and Anne Wyld had been in New Zealand for 4 days and gave a full account of Gary trying to break a pack of 5 over the closing stages. A strong headwind down the back straight didn't help and he paid the penalty. He was inconsolable for a few days but was cheered by the genuine support of the various coaches and sports press who felt it was his best run to date. Marcus Adam only just made the semi-final of the 100. Ron thought him lame but it turned out to be a loose spike plate. A change of shoes and he looked much sharper. The Games, for me, started after 5 hours kip. Sunday January 28th. The Sultan of Brunei had taken a floor of our hotel while our Patron Eddie K had staked his claim with a scattering of coaches and friends. My first pleasant surprise was the transport. Eddie had arranged for 2 stretch limo's - darkened glass, air conditioning, Union and New Zealand flags, the lot - to provide transport for the week. And that set the tone for what was to be a fantastic Games in more ways than one. At the Stadium there was a brief parade and Don Anderson took over the responsibility of siting the Belgrave banner. Advised by former Belgravian Graham Seatter, who was working on the TV commentaries, he did a great job only losing it on the final day as Gary Staines and Andy Lloyd paraded it at the Closing Ceremony. Ron Wyld eventually recovered it from the Games Village so it will still be around this year. On the track the final of the 100 was the highlight. All day the wind down the home straight hovered around 2.3m/s so that most sprint times were not valid for record purposes. John Regis managed a legal personal best, finishing 4th in 10.25 in the second semi-final, while Marcus Adam ran 10.31 to finish second in the 1st semi but easing over the middle 50m. In the final it was a different story with Marcus blasting from the gun in lane one to finish 2-100ths off bronze in a slightly windy legal personal best of 10.14 with John 7th in 10.22. The first day of the Mens Decathlon provided much excitement and in the Womens 3000m Carolyn Schuwalow (Mrs. Andy Lloyd who last summer trained from Belgrave Hall ) ran a splendid personal best of 8:53.89 to finish a creditable 5th. Monday January 29th. The sprinters were back in action with the first and second round of the 200. Marcus was brimming with confidence and John knew he was back at his best. The races were a procession as follows: Round 1 Heat 1. 1st J. Regis 20.80; Heat 6. 1. M.Adam 21.00; Round 2 Heat 2. 1st J. Regis 20.40; Heat 4. M. Adam 20.35. Although windy the opposition were getting worried and the Games record of 20.43 was in danger; if only the wind would drop a bit from that tantalising 2.3 m/s. Following the conclusion of the mens decathlon in which England's late entry Eugene Gilkes gained bronze, we awaited the heats of the 5000m. Belgrave cheers were for Andy Lloyd who finished a comfortable 4th in the second heat in 13:52.63. In the 800 heats and semi's Seb Coe was looking tired and new boy Matthew Yates did what we had seen so many times in last year's British League matches - left it late and kicked with devastating effect over the last 140m to ease into the final. Sadly in the Womens Shot Judy Oakes could only just manage Silver, much to her and our disappointment. Tuesday January 30th. With this day devoted to the Men's Marathon we thought it was the one to watch on TV as all coast roads had been closed to traffic. Not to be beaten, Eddie had hired a Cruiser to follow the race, hopping ashore as appropriate. The limo's arrived at 6.30 and off we went with a fair sprinkling of names; Harry Wilson, Ron Roddan, Chris Brasher, Ann and Ron Wyld, Kevin Reed and so on. Despite misgivings everyone took to the water like hardened seafarers and apart from the marathon we got a guided tour of the Whitbread Round the World yachts which were due to race in the 3rd leg from Auckland the following Sunday - see what I mean about the Eddie experience! Wednesday January 31th. Lisa Martin left them for dead from the gun in the Womens Marathon. We listened to the race on the car radio as the Belgrave contingent drove to Rautarua to view the volcanic activity and spouting 'geezers'. Well thats what we called them until the locals pointed out that 'geezers' came from the East End of London and we had better call them 'guysers'! We hurried back for an evening party for U.K. athletes hosted by Eddie K, President of the Sports Aid Foundation. Guest of honour was President Elect of the Commonwealth Games - HRH Prince Edward. Thursday February 1st. The track and field programme was hotting up with an increasing number of finals. Sadly in the discus Abi Ekoku got it all wrong and had 3 no throws each of them out of the sector to the right. The first and last time we hope. Totally disconsolate, Abi was to learn that Neil Gray had hurt his back and that he would get a 'reprieve' and fill the 3rd England spot in the shot on the closing day. Time enough to get himself sorted out! In the 200 semi's Marcus won the first in 20.33 and John striding effortlessly won the second in 20.35 - both windy but it looked good for the final. Later in the day the final was won by Marcus in a blistering 20.10 and John recording a windy personal best of 20.16, back to his very best; and to complete Englands medal tally Ade Mafe finished third with 20.26 - a truly great race and one of the highlights of the Games for me. By now, Belgravians were homing in on the banner, first Paul Cuff then Charles Dickenson (Surrey Vets C.C. Champ of '88) together with his family came for a chat. They are on a world tour for 2 years and following a stay in the USA are now enjoying their sojourn down under. He's racing well but finding the competition tough. And believe it or not just sitting in front of me one day was Joe Dooley who I trained with at Battersea and last saw 15 years ago. Small world is'nt it? And so to the 800 where Matthew Yates surprised all the critics with an excellent 3rd spot. We still had the 5,000m to look forward to. The event is now history, the series of trips, Ngugi's rush from his fall back into the lead and the thrilling last 200 in 24.2 seconds by Andy Lloyd to give him victory by the narrowest of margins. The Belgrave contingent were hoarse with excitement as the scoreboard proclaimed: 1. A.Lloyd (Aus) 13:24.86, J. Ngugi (Ken) 13;24.94, 3. I. Hamer (Wal) 13:25.63. Another great day! Friday February 2nd. To represent one's Country for the first time, and to set a personal best is all one can hope. But to come away with a Silver medal is just a fairytale - and that fairytale happened to Ian Tullett in the pole vault following a slightly hesitant start in a difficult cross wind. The opposition quickly fell by the wayside as Ian cleared 5.25m to be assured of a medal. New Zealand decathlete Simon Poelman passed 5.25 and failed at 5.30 to give Ian Silver. The bar went to 5.35 and at this height he just failed by the narrowest of margins. Another Belgrave medal. The heats of the 4x100m next with Marcus resting due to a slight groin strain. A red flag on the second handover caused a stir as John Regis was just on the line as Jarrett took the baton, but it was Ghana who were disqualified. Saturday 3rd. Belgrave interest centred on Paul Edwards and Abi Ekoku in the shot. Paul, favourite for a medal did not disappoint with 18.17 for the bronze. But it was Abi who surprised us to throw a personal best in the fourth round with 17.45 for sixth spot. You could just see how that made up for the discus and he could enjoy the celebrations later. Meanwhile in the javelin Nigel Bevan was looking menacing in the warm up throws. His coach Peter Byrne had been supervising his last minute preparations and we had been hearing rumours of 82/83 m efforts. But in this highest level competition the very best would be needed for a medal. Buckley opened with 84.90, Hill with 81.32 and the New Zealand pair pushing 78.00. Nigel could only manage 70.42, improving to 75.66. Going with the last round he found himself in 6th spot and it was here that his competitive nature took over. Everything was perfect as he launched a mighty throw - nearly the last of the competition - which soared towards the 80m mark. The New Zealand spectators held their collective breaths to see if the bronze was safe. It was, but only just, as Nigel's throw was measured at a new personal best of 79.70 to further extend his Welsh record. Marcus came into the England squad for the 4x100 final and despite imperfect changing it was Linford Christie who ensured golds for the squad members in 38.57. The Belgrave medal and points haul had risen to 4 Gold, 2 Silver, 1 Bronze, 3 fourths and a sixth. An achievement which put us top of the England Clubs, ahead of most Countries and one which was beyond our wildest dreams. Well done everyone. And so it was over. A wonderful closing ceremony; totally more exciting than the Television portrayal. For me there are a host of wonderful memories, all pleasant, many amusing. I shan't forget John Bicourt arriving jet lagged at the Games Village in a downpour. The ever friendly Kiwi officials gave him the standard transparent thin blue mac - tight fitting, no arms just a small circle for the face. John was looking for athletes to race in Java. The last we saw of him he was trudging damp and miserable, towards the athletes quarters. Christ! I thought, he's missed his true vocation, he looks like an advert for safer sex! Farewell from the friendly Games. Above : An Eddiemobile. Below : Don Anderson, Bill Laws and Charles Dickenson find things a bit hot!! items.s: PRIORY BLUES Light note on team manager Colin Pearson's reaction to Belgrave's runaway win over Brighton and Hove in the Priory Relays. Team Manager Colin Pearson didn't know whether to laugh or cry after Belgrave's run-away win in the Priory Relays. After a 2 minute victory over Southern Champions Brighton and Hove he was seen pulling out his hair! "What a team! - we could have charged a fortune if this had been televised! - and it didn't cost me a penny!". Colin Pearson Colin Pearson team manager Priory Relays Brighton and Hove

Belgrave race walking review of 1988-89, opening with a season overview and then race-by-race results for the men's and ladies' teams, including Paul King's London to Brighton win and Geoff Fitzgerald becoming a Centurion. The past twelve months have not been a wonderful success, when the ladies have turned out a team they have usually been in the scoring three with Sian Spacey collecting some individual positions. The men have been eratic, when we have had a full team out then we have ususally been placed but for much of the early part of this year that has been seldom. John Hall in his first year as a vet has shown some excellent form, Paul Warburton has been plagued by injury problems and Carl Lawton was off the road for much of the early part of the year. 10TH OCTOBER 1988 CHIPPENHAM TO CALNE 6 MILES Here our ladies placed 3rd with Sian Spacey (6th.52:19), Gill Brackpool (10th.57:28), Sue Morrison (11th,57:50), Karen Barker (13th.59:38). items.sum: Carl Lawton's 1990 update on the walking section, describing a near-empty year with injuries and few walkers and urging members to turn up in 1991.
items.s: 1990 WALKING SECTION UPDATE Carl Lawton's 1990 update on the walking section, describing a near-empty year with injuries and few walkers and urging members to turn up in 1991. Many thought that 1989 was bad. 1990 has been almost non existant. We have been thin on the ground for a couple of years but this year with injury problems to two active walkers has put paid to virtually all team competition and it has been left to Doug Fotheringham and John Dunsford to keep some sort of notification that Belgrave still has a mens side. The ladies have also had problems and we have not done as well as in previous years. One of the problems is getting enough out when they are needed. Being optmistic we could be on the up, we really cannot go any lower, and 1991 could see increased numbers out in both men and womens races. To do this we have to co-ordinate better and endeavour to make a concerted effort to enter races and TURN UP. Carl Lawton Doug Fotheringham Doug Fotheringham kept the men's walking side going in 1990 John Dunsford John Dunsford kept the men's walking side going in 1990 Carl Lawton Carl Lawton

items.sum: Introduction to the track and field section covering 1989 and 1990: steady progress in the British Athletics League, promotions in the Southern League, disappointing cup results and new star signings.
items.s: Track and Field. Introduction to the track and field section covering 1989 and 1990: steady progress in the British Athletics League, promotions in the Southern League, disappointing cup results and new star signings. The last issue of the Belgravian dealt with the 1988 Track and Field season. In the following pages we have compressed the subsequent two years results concentrating mainly on team performances as the fine exploits of many of our top athletes have been recorded elsewhere and will be familiar to you. Our 'A' team continued to make steady progress in Division 1 of the GRE British Athletics League although the team performances never quite achieved the sum total of the individual strengths. In '89 the 'B' team again just missed promotion to Division 1 of the Southern League but finally achieved its aim in 1990. 1989 was the first year we put out a 'C' team in Division 7 of the Southern Lge and it immediately gained promotion to Division 6. It is fair to say that now we can offer anybody summer competition at whatever level is required. Our Cup performances continue to disappoint. Although we have made the finals for 3 consecutive years the attraction of a televised meet does not seem to act as a spur to those just below Super Star standard while the big guns are generally looking for a rest. One day it may all come together! We have been fortunate over the last two seasons in that many of this Country's top athletes have chosen Belgrave as the Club at which they wish to further their careers. In this issue we have given a brief rundown on the new names and we look forward to watching their progress in the years ahead. British Athletics League Southern League

items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Bob Bridges' 1989 Southern League round-up: the 'B' team sixth again and missing promotion to Division 1, the new 'C' team promoted to Division 6.
items.s: SOUTHERN LEAGUE ROUNDUP Bob Bridges' 1989 Southern League round-up: the 'B' team sixth again and missing promotion to Division 1, the new 'C' team promoted to Division 6. First the bad news, once again we have failed to gain promotion to division one. This was the third year running that we have finished sixth, ( the top five gaining promotion ) although it was by the slimest of margins, the same league points as the fifth club but falling short on match pionts. Perhaps 1990 will be our year, I certainly believe we can do it, we just need to be a little more cosistent. Now the good news, our 'C' team won promotion to division six. This was the first season that we have had a 'C' team in the Southern League, so we had to start at the bottom, winning all our matches. This was not always easy with everybody having to cover several unfamilar events, but all enjoying themselves immensely. The age of competitors in this team can vary quite considerably, with father and son competing along side each other on numerous occasions. I would to thank all those who did turn out this season and hope to see you all again next year. A look at the results will show who did what and where. Listed below is the dates and venues for the 1990 season and as can be seen there is not a great deal of travelling to be done, so lets see if both teams can win promotion this coming season. So give me a ring and let me know when you are available and what you would like to do. Bob Bridges Bob Bridges Bob Bridges Southern League team manager Southern League

items.sum: Match-by-match report of Belgrave's 1989 British Athletics League Division 1 season, from 4th and 3rd places to a 7th at Birmingham and safety at Enfield, with John Gladwin's return and Abi and Lenny as top scorers.
items.s: BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE REPORT Match-by-match report of Belgrave's 1989 British Athletics League Division 1 season, from 4th and 3rd places to a 7th at Birmingham and safety at Enfield, with John Gladwin's return and Abi and Lenny as top scorers. 1989. Match 1 Alexander Stadium Birmingham 13 May 1989. A solid start to the new league season with 4th place at the end of the afternoon. Fine wins were recorded by Marcus(200m) and Nigel (Javelin) and by the 4x100 realy team (Lenny,Dave,John,Phil), who showed all the other teams how to run a relay. This 4x100 time and the 4x400 were to be our best times for the season. The most welcome sight was to see John Gladwin back in the Belgrave vest on the track, after a long illness. Nigel and Abi covered all the throws in a busy afternoon. One prediction came true in that we easily beat Haringey! Match 2 Haringey 10 June 1989. Another good result put us third in the league behind Birchfield and Haringey. John Gladwin, running the A string, showed that he is back to his best with a superb win over a good class field. Other wins came from Marcus(200),Simon ( B S/C), Femi ( a magnificent 16.38 TJ), and Andy Hutchinson (HJ). The high jump proved to be our top points event with Ossie and Andy for a 2nd and 1st. Paul Evans led all the way in the 5k to be caught on the line by Steve Harris. The pole vault proved to be controversial with the leading vaulters opting out, because of a dangerous take off box. Jimmy Summers would have none of it and proceeded to finish 4th in the A string and gained more points than in the Hammer! Match 3 Alexander Stadium Birmingham 15 July 1989 With hopes high of consolidating our position we were brought down to earth by a disappointing 7th place, on our 2nd visit to Birmingham. We did not have a bad team on paper, but everybody else was at full strength. Femi and Phil Okoro combined well for a 2nd and 1st in the triple jump. Lenny was a hero with two sprint wins and he was ably backed by Phil Goedluck. Best performance of the day came from Andy Lloyd, who front ran the 1500 and left everybody for dead as he stretched out a very high class field. Marcello made an unbelieveable breakthrough in the chase and was rewarded by being asked to run the 5000, where he finished a brave 6th. Match 4 Enfield 5 August 1989 The final match was switched to Enfield and there was still a possibility that we could be relegated. As it turned out, this proved not to be the case - at one point towards the end of the meeting, it was Blackheath who were looking very worried. We were again hit by having no sprinters to back Lenny - with Phil, Ernest and Mike Bazire injured and John and Marcus competing elsewhere. John Gladwin again won the 800 in a magnificent 1:48.21. Lenny had another sprint double and Andy Lloyd won the 1500 B. Other winners were Abi (DT), and Chris Cornwell (HJ B). Abi proved to be our biggest points scorer and did not miss a match all season including the GRE Cup. Lenny won most points in a match with 33½ at Enfield. They both combined great performances with a great team spirit and were a fine example to everybody. Neil Hammersley and Jay Busk were also ever present all season. A mention should be made of our supporters who supplied liberal heaps of sandwiches throughout the season. This group included Ted from Lowestoft,who will probably have a lot to say for himself once he gets to know everybody! items.sum: Report of Belgrave's 1989 GRE Gold Cup: second place in the Cwmbran semi-final behind Blackheath, then seventh in the final at Stoke-on-Trent.
items.s: GRE GOLD CUP REPORT Report of Belgrave's 1989 GRE Gold Cup: second place in the Cwmbran semi-final behind Blackheath, then seventh in the final at Stoke-on-Trent. Semi Final Cwmbran 30 July 1989 Victims of the dreaded random draw, we were forced to travel down to South Wales and compete against fellow Division One clubs Blackheath and Shaftsbury. The first two teams would progress through to the final. We lay in 5th place for most of the afternoon with steady performances from everybody. Towards the end of the day came 'le grande surge ' and we leapfrogged into 2nd place. This came from wins in the TJ(Femi), Discus(Abi),Javelin(Nigel), and the 4x100 relay team. Highlights of the afternoon were the new club record set by Neil Hammersley, on home soil, in the 400h, breaking Mel Ford's old mark. The 4x400 also ended in excitement with Nigel from Blackheath and Jay fighting out the last leg. This followed a cool 47.5 from Marcus. Blackheath won the Meeting and the relay. Final Stoke-on-Trent This was our 2nd final and with a better looking team we fancied a place at the very least. Unfortunately, it was not to be - Abi got caught up in the dreaded M6 traffic and missed the Discus and we were disqualified in the 4x100 relay, having been yards up at the last change. Our 7th place could so easily have been 2nd or 3rd. Marcus proved to be our only winner with an excellent 200m, but other good performances came from Andy Hutchinson, with a great 2.15 high jump, Paul Evans 2nd place in the 10000 and Femi's 2nd place in the triple jump. Next Year !!! Femi Femi won triple jump in semi-final; 2nd in final Abi Abi won discus in semi-final; missed final discus in M6 traffic Nigel Nigel won javelin in semi-final Neil Hammersley Neil Hammersley new club record 400m hurdles at Cwmbran, breaking Mel Ford's mark Mel Ford Mel Ford previous club 400m hurdles record holder Nigel Nigel Blackheath; 4x400 last leg Jay Jay 4x400 last leg Marcus Marcus 47.5 4x400 leg in semi-final; won 200m in final Andy Hutchinson Andy Hutchinson 2.15 high jump in final Paul Evans Paul Evans 2nd in 10000 in final GRE Gold Cup Cwmbran South Wales Stoke-on-Trent Blackheath Shaftsbury

items.sum: Match-by-match reports of Belgrave's 1990 British Athletics League Division 1 season, finishing third in the league with a record points total.
items.s: GRE BRITISH ATHLETICS LEAGUE - DIVISION 1 REPORTS 1990 Match-by-match reports of Belgrave's 1990 British Athletics League Division 1 season, finishing third in the league with a record points total. Match 1 Depleted in several areas we travelled to Copthall with some trepidation. Fortunately other teams were experiencing similar early season problems and we finished on equal points with Shaftesbury but were awarded 2nd Match place due to our superior number of wins. Lennie Paul was a clear winner in the 'A' 100 and 200, Abi in the 'A' discus, Andy Lloyd in the 'A' 1500, Paul Evans in the 'A' pole vault while Mike Edwards arrived jet lagged straight from the U.S.A. to set a pb and a new Club Record by winning the 'A' pole vault with 5.30. His father, Mike Edwards Senior, did not stand idly bt but scored good points in the 'B' pole vault. Phil Goedluck scored a win in the 'B' 200 and our sprinters surprised Haringey in the 4 x 100 to win with Adrian Carter proving a remarkable substitute for an unfit Marcus Adam. The other notable performance was by one of our remarkable youths - 6 ft. 4 Stanley Osuide finishing second in the 'B' high jump. A quite remarkable debut for this young man in the U.K.'s Premier League. Match 2 Crystal Palace could almost be classified as a home fixture but it proved unlucky. As with most home fixtures athletes made their own transport arrangements and the team managers were reduced to gibbering wrecks as several athletes failed to appear or announced late illness. Badly hit were the sprints with John Regis our only top ranked man losing a tight battle with Linford Christie in the 100. Norman Shute travelled at late notice from Gateshead but travel plus the competition proved quite a problem for him. Our middle distance men rallied well with Darryl Maynard standing in at 20 minutes notice to gain good 800 m points while we won both 1500m's with Stuart Paton gaining a faster win in the 'B' than Andy LLoyd in 'A' - but Andy then ran the 'A' 5000 some 30 minutes later to record a very creditable 14.04. Abi again scored maximum points in the discus and shot and Phil MaKay made a welcome return to ensure a clean sweep in the shot. Our javelin was again below par with Nigel Bevan still sidelined with injury. Mike Edwards junior edged the Club pole vault record higher as he continued his quest for maximum points through the season. All in all the team did well to finish 3rd and held onto 2nd place in the League. Match 3 We travelled to Birmingham in the knowledge that several of ur stars had performed in Edinburgh at the previous night's International Match. Marcus Adam made a game effort to boost our results folloiwng a good performance in Edinburgh but it was soon apparent that lack of deep down fitness had caught him out and he just walked in in the 200. Gary Staines used this match to assess fitness after injury and his winning performance looked good for the future. But the big surpise was Olly Foote winning the 'B' to make it a first time double in BAL Division 1 5000 m's. Another double in the shot but Abi just couldn't master the wind in the discus and settled for second. Our 400 hurdlers produced a record number of points as Paul Beaumont set a new Club Record in his debut while previous record holder Neil Hammersley showed a return to form in the 'B' race. Mike Edwards continued his winning ways in the pole vault and Lenny Paul clocked up two 'B' string sprint wins. Another 3rd place for the team to narrowly maintain our 2nd League place but Birchfield look determined to catch us. Match 4 Our traditional poor start was at least reversed as Phil Spivey made his debut for us to gain 4th place in the hammer followed immediately by a fine 2nd in the 'A' 400H by Paul Beaumont. Neil Hammersley gained his first 'B' 400H win with a sub 53.0 clocking to show there's life in the old dog yet. Our long sprints were a disappointment considering the depth we have in the 200m but Jay Busk performed above expectiations to gain a 4th in the 'A' 400. Other than another fine win for Mike Edwards the highlight was a javelin double win to herald the return to fitness of Nigel Bevan and a new model Jason Bridges who has proved an enthusiastic competitor willing to fill in as required - a boon to team managers which is also exhibited by Darryl Maynard, Ian Wells, Abi Ekoku among others. But despite their support there were too many gaps to prevent us finishing 3rd in the League. Our final points score was some 200 points higher than our previous best. items.s: CIVIL SERVICE/BELGRAVE HARRIERS Report and results of Belgrave athletes competing for the Civil Service in 1989, including the Civil Service Championships at New River Stadium. The unofficial Belgrave club championships were very kindly organised by the Civil Service at New River Stadium on 9 August. Highlight of the day for Belgrave athletes was Ian Well's 5th succesive win in the 400m hurdles, celebrated in a vulgar display of arm waving! Ian also took 2nd in the high hurdles and Jay Busk won the 400m. In the field Chris Cornwell won the high jump and Phil Okoro the long jump. Phil did manage to jump a lot further after the competition but that's another story. Jay Busk also had a hand (leg?) in his department's winning relay team. Belgrave athletes took part in all Civil Service matches and formed a strong part of some very succesful teams although records of results are a little sketchy. items.sum: Light-hearted notice of the marriage of Sue Morrison and Harry Porter, who had long promoted the club's Ladies Section.
items.s: LADIES SECTION AMALGAMATION Light-hearted notice of the marriage of Sue Morrison and Harry Porter, who had long promoted the club's Ladies Section. Sue Morrison and Harry Porter have for years worked hard to promote our Ladies Section. Familiarity has led to wedding bells, and soon after the end of the 1990 Track and Field season the formal amalgamation was declared and a name change registered. Our very best wishes for a long and happy partnership. Sue Morrison Sue Morrison married Harry Porter after the 1990 track and field season Harry Porter Harry Porter married Sue Morrison after the 1990 track and field season

items.label: March 1991
items.sum: Leo Coy's round-up of the young athletes' 1990 track and field season, covering the English Schools high jumpers, the league competitions and each age group.
items.s: Young Athletes. Leo Coy's round-up of the young athletes' 1990 track and field season, covering the English Schools high jumpers, the league competitions and each age group. Round-up 1990 The most outstanding achievements for our track and field season were the performance of our two outstanding high jumpers - Stanley and Sean. They finished first and second in the English Schools Champs and were rewarded by gaining Schools International Caps. They both regularly competed for the British League Team and were instrumental in our B team gaining promotion to Southern League Div. 1. John Abadon also represented his school at the English Schools and also ran for our promotion winning Southern League team. Our season in the Woolworths Young Athletes was somewhat disappointing, our best result was in the first match and after that we steadily went downhill. The Colts section were quite magnificent and almost achieved maximum points in every match. The team spirit among the Colts was really very good and we look forward to this being carried forward into the 1991 season. Peter Lloyd had a magnificent season and narrowly missed breaking the Club record for 800m. He has carried this form into the Winter CC season. The Boys age group also performed well and with a great spirit. For example, Ben Cooper could not run because of injury, so he turned up and threw the javelin. Equally Toby Earle volunteered to throw the hammer and finally succeeded, but it may be for the last time !! The Youths section was weak because of lack of numbers. Stanley and Sean turned out in most matches and we were lucky to find a new sprinter in Rickie. He competed in two YAL matches, as a first year Youth and we look forward to him playing an important role in this year's league matches. The Thameside League was very disappointing with only a very small number of athletes turning out in each match. We could do welll but it would need everybody being committed to turning out in every round. The coming season should be one of our best ever with a lot of new faces in the Boys and Colts sectiosn and a few more Youths to strengthen our team. If everybody pulls together and we cover all events then we will get promoted, so volunteers please for pole vault, hammer, steeplechase, 400h, etc., etc. Finally thanks to Chris Knight for his help and to all the parents who assisted in the field events, with a special thanks to Andrew Hill's Dad for looking after the Thameside League. items.sum: Late report on Belgrave athletes at the 1990 European Championships in Split: John Regis's medals, Gary Staines's 5000m silver, and disappointments for Mike Edwards and Abi Ekoku.
items.s: LATE RESULT Late report on Belgrave athletes at the 1990 European Championships in Split: John Regis's medals, Gary Staines's 5000m silver, and disappointments for Mike Edwards and Abi Ekoku. 27TH AUGUST-1ST SEPT. 1990 XVth EUROPEAN CHAMPIONSHIPS SPLIT KING JOHN As the UK turned the tables on the opposition and finished with a record breaking 9 golds and a total medal tally of 18, the star of the European Championships was John Regis. Bronze in the 100m (10.07w), winner of the 200m in a legal 20.11, silver medal with Marcus in the 4x100 in a new UK record of 37.98, and another gold in the 4x400 with John running an incredible 43.93 split as the quartet sped to a new European record of 2:58.22 In the 5000m Gary Staines lived up to our highest hopes taking the lead with 100m to go, but having to succumb to Antibo's final burst still to finish with a fine silver in 13:22.45. Many of the pole vaulters failed to qualify and among several of the elite who missed the cut was Mike Edwards who only managed a disappointing 5.10. Abi Ekoku also turned in a below par performance with injury reducing his best discuss throw to 53.80. items.label: July 1991
items.h: President of Belgrave Harriers 1990-91 — Win Shepherd writes ...
items.sum: Message from Win Shepherd, Belgrave's first Lady President, with a photo and a short profile by C.D. of her family links to the club and her race walking career.
items.s: President of Belgrave Harriers 1990-91 — Win Shepherd writes ... Message from Win Shepherd, Belgrave's first Lady President, with a photo and a short profile by C.D. of her family links to the club and her race walking career. President of Belgrave Harriers 1990-91 Win Shepherd writes ... It gives me great pleasure to send you this message as your first Lady President. I send my best wishes to you all and hope that you will have a good Walking, Cross Country, Road Racing and Track and Field season. I should like you to remember that you are members of a great club but although you are an individual you are also a member of a team. When you are asked to represent the Club, please do so. Within the club there is a band of officials who work hard for your benefit. At the moment please note that we are very short of officials for track and field meetings. A certain few are keeping things going at home meetings. It would be nice if those of you who have hung up your running shoes would come along and help at the grass roots of Athletics. You will certainly enjoy yourselves! Let's make the rest of 1991 a good year for Belgrave! Win Shepherd Win is caught by the lens of Alex Apperley at a recent Club Championship meeting. Win Shepherd, Belgrave's first Lady President, has been associated with the club since the age of three. Her father, Dick Savage, joined Belgrave in the year 1910 and became President 1944-1946. Her late husband Dave Shepherd, who joined in 1932, was also President in 1962-1963. Win became interested in race walking when she was fifteen years old but as there was no Ladies Section in those days she had to join London Olympiads. She was their Club Champion for three years, Surrey County Champion for three years, and won the Inter-Counties and was second four times whilst representing Surrey. In addition she was twice a member of the Champion National Road Walk team. As you can see, she competed at the highest level. Later, with her mother, Win organised the refreshments at Belgrave Hall on Saturday afternoons for a period of some nine years and when the Ladies Section was formed in 1976 she became our first Ladies Secretary. Win can always be seen at Belgrave meetings either officiating or scoring. With that claret and gold blood in her veins it would be difficult to keep her away! C.D. Win is caught by the lens of Alex Apperley at a recent Club Championship meeting.
